nodes.label: Modular Monolith Architecture
nodes.rationale: The system is designed as a single Next.js application containing well-separated business modules to lower initial complexity while maintaining clear boundaries.

nodes.label: Provider Adapter Layer
nodes.rationale: All external integrations (GitHub, Vercel, Stripe, etc.) must be isolated behind provider adapters to ensure application modules depend on internal interfaces rather than vendor SDKs.

nodes.label: Standard Request Flow
nodes.rationale: Mandatory sequence: Authenticate -> Resolve Identity -> Authorize -> Validate -> Execute Service -> Enforce Rules -> DB/Provider Call -> Audit -> Response.

nodes.label: Durable Job Processing
nodes.rationale: Operations requiring retries or long-running execution must use a durable job mechanism (PostgreSQL-backed or managed queue) rather than in-memory tasks.

nodes.label: Payment Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separates business requests from provider-specific implementations (Stripe/Dojo) using signed webhooks, idempotency, and reconciliation.

nodes.label: Safe DNS Workflow
nodes.rationale: Requires preview, impact warning, explicit confirmation, and post-change verification for high-impact records like NS, MX, and CAA.

nodes.label: WebRTC Signaling & Media
nodes.rationale: Uses Supabase Realtime for authenticated signaling and STUN/TURN for peer media transport; media streams are never stored in the database.

nodes.label: Audit & Observability
nodes.rationale: Mandatory recording of sensitive actions (role changes, DNS mods, payments) with correlation IDs for request/job/provider events.

nodes.label: HR & Salary Architecture
nodes.rationale: Highly sensitive module requiring dedicated permissions; separates general staff management from financial salary records.
